name: 奥の森

meanings: inner part; inside; interior; depths (e.g. of a forest)
inner part; inside; interior; depths (e.g. of a forest)
theme: An ancient, watchful forest of towering silver-barked trees, luminous moss, and drifting spores — deep, still, and alive with unseen presences
description:
The Deep Forest begins where the last trail vanishes beneath a canopy so thick that sunlight only reaches the ground in scattered golden coins. Ancient trees rise like cathedral pillars, their trunks wrapped in soft emerald moss and pale lichen that glows faintly in the perpetual twilight. The bark is silvery-white on the oldest trees, peeling in gentle curls that reveal warm amber heartwood beneath.

The air is cool and still, heavy with the sweet smell of damp earth and wild mushrooms. Shelf fungi in shades of apricot and cream climb the trunks in spiraling staircases, and clusters of luminous spores drift lazily between the branches like tiny lanterns set loose by an unseen hand. Thick roots weave across the forest floor in knotted bridges, carpeted with clover and tiny star-shaped white flowers that seem to pulse with a faint inner warmth.

Deeper in, the canopy opens into rare clearings where shafts of honey-gold light pour down through gaps in the leaves, illuminating curtains of floating pollen and seed fluff. Fallen trees rest on their sides like sleeping giants, their hollowed cores glowing with bioluminescent moss in shades of soft teal and warm peach. Spider silk catches the light between branches, each strand beaded with dew that refracts tiny rainbows.

Birdsong echoes from somewhere high and unseen. Fern fronds as tall as a person unfurl along stream banks where clear water runs over smooth, tea-colored stones. Occasionally the canopy rustles with movement — a branch swaying where nothing visible touched it, a shadow slipping between trunks just at the edge of perception. The forest watches, patient and ancient, not threatening but deeply aware of everything that steps beneath its branches.

name: 静かな公園
theme: A sun-dappled Japanese park with flower beds, a koi pond, arched bridges, and spirit wisps drifting among the blossoms
description:
The park opens up as a wide, sun-dappled clearing framed by rows of mature cherry and zelkova trees whose branches arch overhead in a loose, leafy vault. Warm afternoon light pours through the canopy in broad golden shafts, dappling the gravel paths and wide lawns in shifting patterns of amber and cool green shadow. The grass is impossibly lush — a deep emerald carpet scattered with tiny white clover flowers and the occasional patch of wild violets.

A central pond anchors the space, its surface glassy and still except where fat orange koi break the surface in lazy circles. Lily pads crowd the shallows, their waxy leaves supporting delicate pink and white blooms. A graceful arched wooden bridge, its planks worn smooth by generations of footsteps, crosses the narrowest point. Flat stepping stones lead from the bridge to a mossy bank where the water is shallow and clear enough to see polished river stones on the bottom.

Flower beds line the walking paths in exuberant rows — tulips, marigolds, and hydrangeas in every shade from butter yellow to deep indigo, their petals catching the light like stained glass. Wooden benches with peeling green paint sit at intervals along the paths, shaded by spreading magnolia trees heavy with creamy blossoms. A weathered stone lantern stands at a fork in the path, its surface softened by decades of lichen and rain.

The air is warm and sweet with the scent of cut grass and blooming wisteria. Dandelion seeds drift on gentle thermals, spiraling upward in lazy columns of white fluff. Somewhere nearby, water trickles from a bamboo fountain into a stone basin with a rhythmic hollow knock. Spirit wisps — tiny motes of pale gold and soft green — float among the flower beds like pollen given consciousness, drawn to the park's quiet, contented energy. The whole space hums with the peaceful magic of a place that has been loved and tended for a very long time.

name: 秘密の図書館
theme: A hidden library that appears only to those meant to find it — an impossible spiral tower of warm wood and sandstone, filled with floating lanterns, self-turning pages, and whispering books
description:
The Secret Library hides behind a door that wasn't there a moment ago — a narrow oak entrance set into a wall of ivy-covered stone, its brass handle warm to the touch. Inside, the space opens impossibly wide, a great circular tower of honey-colored wood and warm sandstone whose shelves spiral upward along curved walls in an endless helix, disappearing into a soft golden haze far overhead. Thousands of books line every surface — leather-bound volumes in deep burgundy, forest green, and faded indigo, their gilded spines catching the light from dozens of floating paper lanterns that drift lazily between the shelves like luminous jellyfish.

The air smells of old parchment, cedar, and something faintly sweet, like dried flowers pressed between pages centuries ago. At the ground level, the floor is a mosaic of warm terracotta tiles arranged in a compass-rose pattern, scattered with plush reading cushions in muted coral and cream. Low tables of dark polished wood hold open atlases and illustrated bestiaries, their pages turning slowly on their own as if an invisible reader is browsing. Stained-glass windows set high in the tower walls cast pools of amber, rose, and sage-green light that shift across the floor as the sun moves, painting the space in slow-moving watercolors.

Narrow wooden ladders on brass rails connect the spiraling levels, and small balconies jut out at irregular intervals, each one furnished with a single armchair and a reading lamp. Loose pages occasionally detach from their bindings and flutter through the open central shaft like paper butterflies, drifting on warm updrafts before settling onto a different shelf entirely. Certain sections are roped off with velvet cord — not to keep visitors out, but because the books behind them whisper too loudly if disturbed. Dust motes drift through the lantern light like flecks of gold leaf, and the whole tower hums with a deep, contented quiet — the particular silence of a place that chose to be found by you, just this once.

name: 隠れた浜

meanings: to hide; to be hidden; to conceal oneself; to disappear

theme: A secret crescent cove hidden behind sea cliffs, accessible only through a narrow passage at low tide — sheltered, sun-drenched, and teeming with spirit-touched marine life
description:
The entrance reveals itself only at low tide — a narrow cleft in a wall of sea-smoothed basalt, just wide enough to slip through sideways. Beyond the passage, the cliff walls open into a wide crescent cove that the ocean has spent centuries carving in secret. The sand is pale gold, fine as powdered sugar, scattered with fragments of sea glass in soft greens and blues that have been tumbled round by the waves. Shallow tidal pools dot the rocky shelves at either end of the cove, each one a miniature world of pink anemones, jade-green algae, and smooth stones polished to a satin finish.

The water itself is impossibly clear — a gradient from pale turquoise at the shallows to deep sapphire where the cove drops off into open ocean through an underwater channel between the cliffs. Sunlight pours in from above, the cliffs framing a wide ribbon of sky, and where the light hits the water it sends rippling caustic patterns dancing across the rock walls in slow, hypnotic waves of white and gold. Sea spray drifts on warm updrafts, catching the light in brief prismatic flashes.

Stubborn vegetation clings to every ledge and crevice in the cliff face — trailing vines heavy with small white star-shaped flowers, tufts of sea grass, and clusters of succulents in dusty rose and sage. Higher up, a few wind-bent trees lean out over the water, their roots gripping the rock like fingers, dropping the occasional leaf to spiral down into the cove. Tide-line driftwood, bleached silver by the sun, rests in sculptural tangles along the high-water mark.

A faint, warm mist hangs just above the water's surface in the early hours, glowing where the light catches it. Spirit wisps — tiny motes of soft aquamarine — drift above the tide pools like luminous sea foam given flight, drawn to the concentrated life in the sheltered water. The air smells of salt, warm stone, and something faintly sweet, like sun-dried seaweed and wild coastal flowers. The only sounds are the rhythmic lap of gentle waves, the occasional hollow echo off the cliff walls, and the distant cry of unseen seabirds circling far above.

name: 魔法の学校
theme: A traditional Japanese school building enchanted with gentle magic — floating lanterns, luminous chalk, self-folding nets, and a rooftop where piano notes rise as golden motes
description:
The Magic School stands at the top of a terraced hill, its entrance framed by a wide stone arch draped in flowering wisteria that blooms in impossible colors — soft gold, pale rose, and shimmering silver. The main building follows the shape of a traditional Japanese school — long, three-storied, with tall windows — but built from warm sandstone and polished timber instead of concrete, every surface etched with faint sigils that catch the light at odd angles.

Inside, the hallways are wide and sun-flooded, their wooden floors worn smooth by generations of hurrying feet. Shoe cubbies line the entryway in neat rows, some glowing faintly where a student left a charm behind. Floating paper lanterns in pale amber drift along the ceiling at walking pace, casting warm pools of light that follow anyone who passes beneath them. Classroom doors stand open, revealing desks arranged in tidy grids beneath chalkboards where yesterday's equations still shimmer — the chalk itself luminous, the diagrams slowly rotating in place like living blueprints.

The school garden sprawls behind the main building in a riot of overgrown enchantment. Sunflowers track movement instead of sunlight, turning their broad faces to follow passersby. Morning glories climb wire trellises and open their blooms in sequence like a slow wave. A small wooden rabbit hutch sits in one corner surrounded by clover that grows in spiraling patterns, and nearby, a weathered equipment shed leans against the gymnasium wall, its sliding door ajar to reveal stacked floor mats and nets that fold themselves when no one is looking.

On the rooftop, a low stone wall encloses a broad open space where the sky feels enormous and near. The wind carries the faint melody of a music room piano drifting up through open windows below, the notes occasionally visible as tiny motes of golden light rising from the instrument. Spirit wisps in soft amber and pale green float lazily above the stairwell. The whole building hums with the quiet, hopeful energy of a place where knowledge is alive — chalk dust and cherry blossoms, warm light and the echo of bells.

subAreas.name: 広い教室
subAreas.description: A wide, sun-filled classroom with rows of wooden desks arranged in neat grids beneath a high ceiling. Tall windows line one wall, letting in broad shafts of morning light that warm the polished floorboards. A large chalkboard dominates the front wall, faint traces of yesterday's lesson still shimmering in luminous chalk. Paper cranes dangle from strings tied to the ceiling beams, turning slowly in the draft from an open window.

subAreas.name: 長い廊下
subAreas.description: A stretching corridor of polished hardwood that runs the full length of the school building. Shoe-lockers and notice boards line both sides, and floating paper lanterns in pale amber drift along the ceiling at walking pace. Afternoon light pours through evenly spaced windows, casting long golden rectangles across the floor. The faint echo of footsteps carries from somewhere around the next corner.

subAreas.name: 高い屋上
subAreas.description: A broad open rooftop enclosed by a low stone wall, high above the school grounds. The sky feels enormous and close, stretching in every direction over terraced hills and distant treelines. Wind carries the faint melody of a piano drifting up through open windows below, the notes occasionally visible as tiny motes of golden light. Spirit wisps in soft amber and pale green float lazily above the stairwell entrance.

subAreas.name: 小さな中庭
subAreas.description: A quiet inner garden tucked between the school's main building and its gymnasium wing. A single cherry tree stands at the center, its branches draped over a weathered wooden bench. Clover grows in spiraling patterns across the flagstone path, and a small rabbit hutch sits in one corner surrounded by potted herbs. The walls of the surrounding buildings block most of the wind, making the courtyard feel sheltered and still.

subAreas.name: 古い体育館
subAreas.description: A large, echo-filled gymnasium with a high arched ceiling and a worn wooden floor marked with faded court lines. Stacked floor mats lean against one wall beside a rack of bamboo practice swords, and a climbing rope hangs motionless from a steel beam overhead. The windows are set high, letting in dusty shafts of light that catch on the chalk powder still lingering in the air from the last class. A storage room door at the far end stands slightly ajar, revealing folded nets that slowly fold themselves when no one is watching.

subAreas.name: 不思議な図書館
subAreas.description: Towering shelves of enchanted books line every wall, their spines glowing faintly with arcane script. Dust motes drift through shafts of light from tall arched windows, and the air smells of old paper and ink. Somewhere deep among the stacks, pages rustle on their own.

subAreas.name: 美味しい食堂
subAreas.description: A warm, bustling dining hall filled with long wooden tables and the aroma of freshly cooked meals. Enchanted serving trays glide between the kitchen and the seats, delivering steaming bowls and plates. Chatter and laughter fill the high-ceilinged room, punctuated by the occasional clatter of dropped chopsticks.

subAreas.name: 地味な小学校
subAreas.reading: じみなしょうがっこう
subAreas.description: A bright, cheerful wing of the school with smaller desks and colorful drawings pinned to every surface. The rooms here feel simpler and more welcoming, with wide windows letting in plenty of sunlight. Young students' practice spells have left harmless sparkle marks on the walls and ceiling.

subAreas.name: 新しい高校
subAreas.description: A recently constructed wing with clean lines and polished floors that still smell faintly of fresh varnish. The hallways are wide and well-lit by tall rectangular windows set into pale concrete walls, and rows of steel lockers line both sides, some decorated with stickers and small paper charms left by their owners. Homeroom classrooms have sliding doors that glide on smooth tracks, revealing clusters of newer wooden desks with built-in shelves underneath. A glass-walled corridor connects the wing to the main building, offering a view of the school garden below where clubs practice after hours. The notice boards are layered thick with flyers — sports tournaments, festival committees, study groups — pinned over older flyers in an ever-growing collage. At the end of the second floor, a music room leaks faint piano notes through its soundproofed door, and a trophy case at the main stairwell landing holds polished cups and ribbons from recent competitions. Everything here feels modern and cared-for, the wood still pale, the paint unchipped, the brass door handles not yet worn smooth by years of use.

subAreas.name: 立派な大学
subAreas.description: The university wing rises behind the main school building, connected by a covered stone walkway lined with climbing ivy. Its entrance is a pair of tall oak doors beneath a carved stone arch, and stepping through reveals a vaulted atrium floored in dark polished wood that echoes with each footstep. Lecture halls are arranged in steep tiered semicircles, their curved desks worn dark and smooth from generations of note-taking, each seat fitted with a small brass reading lamp. Tall bookshelves line the corridors between rooms, stuffed with thick volumes and rolled parchment tied with colored thread. On the top floor, a research laboratory stretches the full length of the wing — wide tables cluttered with crystal prisms, brass measuring instruments, and open notebooks where ink diagrams continue drawing themselves long after the pen was set down. The hallway ceilings are higher here than anywhere else in the school, and floating lanterns burn a cooler, steadier white light instead of the warm amber found elsewhere. Framed portraits of past headmasters and distinguished scholars hang along the main corridor, their painted eyes following anyone who passes with patient, knowing expressions.
